newsitem.title: USA: Minnesota soybean harvest 95 percent complete.
newsitem.headline: Minnesota soybean harvest 95 percent complete.

text.p: Fall harvesting was slowed by widespread rainfall the week ended Sunday, according to the Minnesota Agricultural Statistics Service.
There were 4.8 days suitable for fieldwork.
Soybean harvesting was complete on 95 percent of the acreage, compared with 81 percent last week, 71 percent a year ago and 80 percent for the five year average.

Corn harvest was 25 percent complete, compared with 15 percent last week, 54 percent last year and the 36-percent average. Moisture content for the harvested corn averaged 25 percent, down from 29 percent last week, but up from 21 percent a year ago. Average moisture content the past five years has been 24 percent.
Sunflowers were 66 percent harvested. Last week's comparison was not available. Sunflower harvesting last year was 69 percent complete and the average was 63 percent.
Sugarbeets were 99 percent harvested, ahead of average pace of 83 percent.
Pasture and range rated nine percent very poor, 23 percent poor, 44 fair, 23 percent good and one percent excellent.
Topsoil moisture was rated three percent very short, 19 short, 57 adequate and 21 surplus.
